body.note: Length, width and height are the published figures for protection level C (7.6 x 4.0 x 3.6 m); the hull and turret boxes, track contact length and gauge are game values.

mass.note: 43 t at protection level C, the combat configuration (31.45 t at level A).

drive.note: Engine power 800 kW (MTU V10 892) and road speed 70 km/h are published; reverse speed, gear bands, efficiency, braking, steering, idle power and fuel use are game values.

ramp.note: Game value (M7), not in the public sources; tuned in the drive lab.

stations.note: Unmanned turret; rates, limits and errors are game values. M7.3: MK30-2/ABM with two ready feeds (armour-piercing and high explosive, 100 each) and the coaxial MG5 (1000 ready). Owner Q17: the ready belts are refilled from stowage in battle, halted, in about 90 s.

vehicles.note: Schuetzenpanzer Puma: 3 crew (commander, gunner, driver in the hull) and 6 dismounts (published). Armour, components and signature come with M7.3/M7.4. M7.2: stowed rifle magazines and machine-gun belts for the squad (game values, low): the men refill from a halted vehicle. M7.3: gun, coaxial machine gun, 30 mm and coax stowage (game split of the published totals), 16 smoke grenades, seat sights (commander panoramic day and thermal, gunner day and thermal following the turret). The driver (buttoned up, owner Q5) drives and does not search for the enemy (game value). M9.3a: MELLS (Spike LR) on the turret, two ready and two more stowed (low), reloaded from outside by a crewman on the roof; a laser warning receiver (low: part of the Puma's protection suite in search extracts).

dischargers.note: 76 mm smoke dischargers on the turret: salvo size, number, arc, range, delay and cloud are game values.

signature.note: Game values: the area comes from the hull and turret boxes; type known within 1.5 km (owner Q6); engine heard 400 m idling, 1200 m driving.

armour.note: Game values. Public descriptions (search extracts only; the pages could not be opened here) give protection level C (43 t, add-on composite modules) as proof of the frontal arc against medium-calibre (30 mm) armour-piercing rounds and of the whole vehicle against 14.5 mm and fragments, and say the add-on modules also protect against hand-held shaped charges. Owner decision Q21 (b), 2026-11-12: the FRONT stops a single PG-7VL (625 mm mild-steel equivalent = 500 mm RHA x 1.25): hull front 150 mm and turret front 140 mm of composite at 60 degrees give 750 / 700 mm against a jet head on (resistance 2.5 per mm) and 480 / 448 mm against kinetic rounds (1.6 per mm); sides and rear (30 mm composite, 48 / 75 mm; turret rear 26 mm) stop 14.5 mm all round as published for the basic protection; roof are penetrated by a PG-7VL; sides stop 14.5 mm but not 30 mm APDS at battle ranges. One plate per part and face (no upper/lower glacis, no spaced skirts).

components.note: Game values: where the engine (front right), tracks, gun, ready ammunition (in the unmanned turret) and fuel lie, how much a round must have left to wreck each, what passing through costs it, and the chance that a penetrating hit on fuel or ammunition starts a fire or blows the ammunition up. M7.4b: transmission, turret drive, stabiliser, coaxial MG, sights, radio, smoke dischargers and extinguisher added (where they commonly sit; boxes and toughness are game values).

extinguisher.note: Game values: the Puma has an automatic fire suppression system (search extracts); its charges, the delay and the chance to put a fire out are not published.

repair.note: M11.7a field repair: the kit the crew needs and the parts each crew task uses up (game values from forum and test-drive search extracts, research 2026-11-16, low).

body.note: Boxer 8x8: length 7.93 m, width 2.99 m (army-technology; search extracts only); roof height of the ambulance module 2.94 m (army-technology; joint-forces gives 8.33 x 3.0 x 3.36 m, probably over fittings). The hull box and the effective steering wheelbase (front axle pair to rear axle pair, for the one-track steering model) are game values.

mass.note: Gross weight 35,000 kg for the ambulance (joint-forces, search extract).

drive.note: MTU V8 of 530 kW (KNDS) and a top speed of 100 km/h (ARTEC; army-technology: over 100 km/h) are published. Seven forward gear bands (an automatic gearbox), reverse speed, braking, steering (about 25 m turning circle), idle power and fuel use are game values (low).

ramp.note: Game values: one rear ramp (with a door); loading a casualty is slower than mounting (stretcher handling, M10.6a decides how it is used).

signature.note: Game values: a high, slab-sided hull; quieter than the tracked carriers (wheels, no track noise).

armour.note: The Boxer's modular armour is classified; search extracts describe protection against heavy machine-gun fire (about 14.5 mm) over the frontal arc and artillery fragments all round. Expressed as armour-steel equivalents: front 30 mm at 50 degrees (stops 12.7 mm AP and most 14.5 mm at range), sides 25 mm (stop 7.62 mm AP and 12.7 mm ball at range), rear 20, roof 12. Every cannon round and rocket in the game penetrates.

components.note: Game values: the drive module sits at the front right (driver front left), the mission module behind it; boxes, toughness and chances are game values. 'wheels': each side's running gear (run-flat tyres; a wrecked side immobilises it).

extinguisher.note: Game values as the Puma's: an automatic fire suppression system is usual on the Boxer; charges, delay and chance are not published.

ambulance.note: Boxer ambulance (Sanitaetskraftfahrzeug): crew of three (driver, commander or doctor, medic; ARTEC brochure) and 7 seated or 3 lying casualties, or 2 lying and 3 seated (search extracts only). Unarmed apart from the crew's rifles; marked with the red cross.

vehicles.note: Boxer ambulance (M10.6-data): the first German wheeled vehicle. Crew of three: commander, driver and a medic in the patient compartment (seat 'med', a crew seat of the generic kind 'loader': no weapon uses it, and he can take over the driving); seats p1-p7 are the sitting places. No weapon station. M7.6b reuses this hull for the Boxer carrier. Ambulance behaviour (requests, runs, loading casualties) comes with M10.6a.

repair.note: M11.7a field repair: the kit the crew needs and the parts each crew task uses up (game values from forum and test-drive search extracts, research 2026-11-16, low).

body.note: Width 3.77 m (KNDS 3.77-4.00 m; 3.81 Army Recognition) and height about 3.0 m to the turret roof (published, medium). The hull length (7.7 m, about 11 m with the gun forward), the boxes, the clearance, the track contact length and gauge are game values from the published overall figures. The gun reaches 4.9 m past the turret front (L/55 tube about 6.6 m).

drive.note: MTU MB 873 Ka-501, 1100 kW (published); top speed 63 km/h (Bundeswehr; KNDS up to 70); reverse 31 km/h (the usually quoted Leopard 2 figure, from memory, low). Gear bands, efficiency, braking, steering, idle power and fuel use are game values (low), tuned in the drive lab.

ramp.note: Game values (M7.6a): no ramp; the crew gets in and out through the hatches (exits beside the hull at the turret).

stations.note: Two-plane stabilised turret with EMES 15 sight and laser rangefinder, PERI hunter-killer commander's sight (published, medium). The 15 rounds in the turret bustle behind blow-out panels (ready: 10 DM63A1, 5 DM11) and 27 in the hull rack beside the driver: 42 in all (published total; the split is common but not confirmed, low). One round loaded at a time by the loader, 6 s sustained (low: 4.4-5 s best, 7.5-8.6 s in older manuals); without him the commander loads, 2.5 times slower (game value). A round is in the breech at the start. Traverse and elevation rates (not found), -9 to +20 degrees, errors and tolerance are game values. Refilling the bustle from the hull rack, halted: 120 s (game value).

dischargers.note: 76 mm Wegmann dischargers, six a turret side on the 2A7V (published; other sources say eight or four): two salvos of six. Range, arc, delay and cloud are game values as the Puma's.

armour.note: Game values from public estimates only (armour is classified; game wikis and forums): line-of-sight equivalents at 0 degrees, one plate per face. Turret front about 850 mm RHA against long rods / 1450-1800 against jets (850 mm of heavy composite: 1062 / 1785 mm mild steel); hull front (upper glacis with the add-on module) about 650 / 1000+ (640 mm: 800 / 1344); hull side about 130 / 200 (100 mm composite: 160 / 250; the heavy front third of the skirts is not separate); turret side 200 / 340 (250 / 420); rear 40-50 mm steel; roof 30 mm steel on the hull, 60 mm composite on the turret (the 2A7V's roof modules). Known simplification: no weaker lower glacis or mantlet.

components.note: Game values: engine and transmission at the rear, ammunition in the turret bustle behind blow-out panels (rarely blows up: cook-off 0.05) and in the hull rack left of the driver (cook-off 0.35), fuel front right; boxes, toughness and chances are game values.

extinguisher.note: Game values: automatic fire suppression (charges, delay and chance are not published).

signature.note: Game values: larger than the Puma's hull and turret boxes alone show (size 1.15); type known within 2 km.

vehicles.note: Leopard 2A7V main battle tank (M7.6a): 4 crew (commander, gunner and loader in the turret, driver front right). Search extracts only (pages not opened in this container). Published (medium): mass, engine, top speed, crew, 42 rounds, sights. Game values (low): armour, components, reload, stowage split, signature. No reactive armour; no active protection (the 2A8 with Trophy comes with M14.5; DM73 later). No laser warner (not found for the 2A7V).

vehicles.note: GTK Boxer GTFz (Gruppentransportfahrzeug), A2 standard, with the KNDS FLW 200 and a 12.7 mm sMG (M7.6c, slice 41): the Jaeger battalions' group carrier (Bundeswehr GTK page, esut.de; search extracts only). Crew of two (driver; commander working the remote weapon station) and eight dismounts: the Bundeswehr page gives at most ten persons (spec sites '3 (+8)'; the 2 + 8 split is an inference, low). Infantry stowage as the Puma's (game value, low). The RCT30 Schwerer Waffentraeger is a different vehicle (no dismounts) and is not modelled.

dischargers.note: The FLW 200's optional MPL 76 mm module with six launchers (KNDS); the German GTK fit is not confirmed (low). Two salvos, range, delay and cloud are game values as the Puma's.

recovery.note: M11.7b: tows up to 70 t (MLC 70; search extracts: 'tows 62 t / MLC 70', the A2 'recovers up to 60 t, MLC 80'; in service it tows the Leopard 2, 64 t: so 70 t, medium for the practice, low for the figure). Tow speed 8 km/h on a rigid bar across country (US recovery manuals: cable 8-16 km/h, bar up to 25 km/h on roads; low). Hook-up 120 s by one man outside (a rigid bar on the Leopard 2 hitch; the WiSENT-type combat recovery hitch needs no man outside at all; research 2-5 min with dismounts: game value, low).

vehicles.note: Bergepanzer 3 Bueffel (M11.7b): the Bundeswehr's armoured recovery vehicle on the Leopard 2 chassis (crane 30 t, main winch 35 t, dozer blade; search extracts, medium). Unarmed in the game (its MG3 is left out, D11): an off-map asset called from the battalion's recovery troop (Bergetrupp Kette), outside the side's strength. Crew of three: two in peacetime plus a seat (search extracts); the game fills the third seat (low).
